excerpt_139_words: Economic, social, and cultural rights protect the material, social, and cultural conditions necessary for human dignity. This article explains the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, progressive realization, maximum available resources, minimum core obligations, non-retrogression, non-discrimination, labor rights, social security, food, water, housing, health, education, cultural participation, science, self-determination, development, and state responsibility. It examines the Committee on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, the Optional Protocol, domestic implementation, justiciability, remedies, budgets, austerity, debt, sanctions, climate change, corporate power, digital systems, and unequal development. By connecting doctrine, institutions, case studies, and lawyer-facing workflows, it shows how economic, social, and cultural rights transform human rights from formal liberty into material dignity while remaining contested by resource scarcity, political choice, and structural inequality worldwide.
